subject: Career
title: The Total Compensation Mindset
description: A fast breakdown of The Total Compensation Mindset for builders.

hook.text: She turned down the $120K offer for the $110K one. Everyone thought she was crazy. But the second had $40K in equity.

buildup.text: Salary is just one piece. Total compensation includes equity, bonuses, benefits, PTO, and growth opportunities.

discovery.text: At senior levels, base salary may be less than 50% of total compensation. Ignoring the rest leaves money on the table.

twist.text: Some benefits have massive hidden value: employer 401K match is free money. Good insurance saves thousands.

climax.text: Always calculate total compensation before comparing offers. A spreadsheet that values each component reveals the truth.

punchline.text: Salary is the headline. Total compensation is the story.

quiz.question: At senior levels, how much of total compensation might base salary represent?

details.summary: Total compensation includes base salary, bonuses, equity, retirement contributions, health benefits, paid time off, and professional development budgets. Evaluating only base salary ignores components that can easily comprise thirty to fifty percent of total value.
details.whyItMatters: Focusing solely on base salary often leaves significant value uncaptured. Candidates who negotiate total compensation packages frequently secure thousands more in overlooked areas.
takeaways: Base salary is only one piece of total compensation
Benefits and equity can add thirty to fifty percent of value
Create a spreadsheet comparing every component across offers

faq.question: What components should I include when calculating total compensation?
faq.answer: Include base salary, annual bonus, signing bonus, equity or stock grants, 401k match, health insurance premiums, HSA contributions, PTO value, remote work stipends, education budgets, and any relocation assistance.

faq.question: How do I compare equity across different company stages?
faq.answer: For public companies, use current stock price times shares. For startups, estimate using the latest 409A valuation and consider the strike price, vesting schedule, and dilution risk. Public equity is generally more liquid and predictable.
